note: Issue 396, policy.md sections 7 and 8, patrons.md sections 3 and 10. A patron whose specialty is resources or livestock names one kind of it, and he can have his Barony buy that kind from the colony rather than from its neighbour: the Crown's price for it goes up while the policy stands. He writes; the PC answers (section 10 lock). The charge and who bears it are policy.md's; 90 a month is a placeholder (section 9). Placeholder prose: the Author writes the real lines.

body.text: My people at home buy a great deal of {param:resource}, and they buy it from a neighbour of ours whom I have never much cared for.

I could have them buy yours instead. It would take some arranging, and some expense, and the Crown would find it was paying rather more for {param:resource} than it is used to. Your colony would not complain.
I should want the Crown to meet the charge of it. I am generous, but I am not a charity.
I should want the Crown to meet the charge of it. I do not suppose that will surprise you.

options.label: accept, and the Crown bears the charge
options.text: Do it, and let the Crown bear the whole of the charge. I would not have you out of pocket for a kindness to my colony.

options.label: accept, and the Crown bears half
options.text: Do it, and the Crown will meet half the charge. I will not pretend that is generous.

options.label: decline, with thanks
options.text: I must decline, and I am sorry to. The Crown has no room for another charge this year.
